title: Pre-Analysis — Titanium Seat Track Attachment Fittings on the Upper Deck
abstract: Closed pre-analysis for the change of the upper deck seat track attachment fittings to titanium, covering the earlier sealed track standard, its retrofit bulletin, the published splice repair and the corrosion inspection task.

sections.objective: Establish the relationship between the proposed titanium attachment fitting and the sealed track sections already retrofitted on part of the fleet, and determine whether the two standards can coexist in the same bay or whether one supersedes the other. The order also had to settle the galvanic question raised by the materials office, since the titanium lug sits against an aluminium track web with a fastener pattern that was never qualified for a dissimilar metal pair in a bay that sees standing water.
sections.findings_summary: Five items were confirmed and one blocked release until it was resolved. The sealed track standard and the titanium fitting cannot coexist on the same track section: the sealed section is machined with a lug seat the titanium fitting does not match, so the earlier standard is superseded rather than complemented wherever the fitting is installed. Its retrofit bulletin remains open on part of the fleet and would send a mechanic to fit a lug that no longer belongs there. The published splice repair uses the steel lug fastener pattern and would put a steel fastener through a titanium lug into an aluminium web, which the materials office would not accept without a wet assembly instruction. The corrosion inspection interval was written for steel lugs and is conservative for titanium. A fifth item was recorded from the similarity pass alone.
sections.next_steps: Release was authorised once the supersession was accepted and the earlier bulletin scheduled for withdrawal on the aircraft that take the fitting. The repair scheme owner was asked to publish a titanium variant of the splice repair with a wet assembly instruction and a revised fastener specification. The inspection interval for titanium bays was left unchanged pending two years of in service evidence, on the argument that the conservative interval costs little and the fleet has no history with the pairing.

similarity_seeds: dissimilar metal pairing at a cabin floor attachment
seat track attachment lug replacement in the galley bays

tasks.title: Establish the interaction with the sealed track standard
Assess the galvanic pairing and the fastener specification
Search published repairs and inspections on the upper deck tracks
Check the open retrofit bulletin position across the fleet

expected_findings.rationale: The sealed track section is machined with a lug seat that matches the steel fitting only. Where the titanium fitting is installed the sealed section has to be re-machined or replaced, so the two standards cannot coexist in the same bay and the earlier modification is superseded rather than complemented.
expected_findings.resolution: Declare the supersession explicitly in the modification and state the rework required on aircraft that already carry sealed sections.

expected_findings.rationale: The sealed section bulletin is still open on roughly a third of the fleet. On an aircraft that has taken the titanium fitting its accomplishment instructions would have a mechanic fit a lug seat that no longer belongs there, and its material list orders items that are no longer correct for that bay.
expected_findings.resolution: Schedule the bulletin for withdrawal on aircraft that take the fitting, and add a pre-accomplishment check of the fitting standard to its effectivity statement.

expected_findings.rationale: The splice repair specifies the steel lug fastener pattern and a dry assembly. Applied over a titanium fitting it would put a steel fastener through a titanium lug into an aluminium web in a bay that sees standing water, which the materials office will not accept.
expected_findings.resolution: Publish a titanium variant of the repair with a wet assembly instruction and a revised fastener specification, before the first retrofit slot.

expected_findings.rationale: The corrosion inspection interval and its acceptance criteria were written for steel lugs. They remain valid but conservative for titanium, and the task text refers to corrosion products the titanium fitting cannot produce.
expected_findings.resolution: Leave the interval unchanged pending in service evidence, but correct the description of the expected findings at the next revision.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity alone. The repair talks about a crack arrest hole and an angle reinforcement at a beam web; the modification talks about a stiffer attachment fitting. They share no identifier and no chapter, but the repair's reasoning about local stiffness at the beam to track junction is the same argument the fitting change makes from the other side.

expected_findings.rationale: A bay that carries the beam web reinforcement and then takes the stiffer titanium fitting sees a stiffness step at the same junction. The stress office asked for the two to be embodied in the same slot wherever both apply, so that the junction is assessed once.
expected_findings.resolution: Record a concurrency note in the modification for bays that already carry the beam web repair.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the upper deck seat zone and reads as a seat installation task, which puts it high on both the entity and the similarity pass. It installs the seat group power distribution unit under the seat and never touches the track attachment fitting or its lug seat.

type_data.conclusion: Issued 2018-12-11. One supersession accepted, one open bulletin scheduled for withdrawal and one repair variant to be published. Cleared to proceed on those three conditions.
